description: A route table whose paths are written the way real ones are. The described-route shape was recognised and matched 109 of one application's 208 descriptions -- 52%, which reads as coverage rather than as a sample, and four of that application's eight true findings lived in files it skipped entirely. The cause was not the shape: 39 of the misses spell the router's own mount point as `path: ''` and were rejected by a truthiness test, 39 name a constant declared at the top of the same file, and 21 build one from a constant. All three resolve through the same helper every other registrar in this frontend already uses. The surface is the assertion here and there are no taint findings on purpose, so anything reported would be a false positive. `<unresolved:prefix>` is deliberate and is the honest answer where the address depends on something the file does not state -- it names the expression that stood in the way rather than claiming `*`. The two negatives are the shapes that describe a route and are not one: an outbound HTTP request configured with a method and a path, and a description whose handler resolves to nothing.
